title: Sue Cleaver hails Victoria Wood legacy as she joins Dinnerladies stage tour

evidence_packet.title: Sue Cleaver hails Victoria Wood legacy as she joins Dinnerladies stage tour
evidence_packet.lead: The stage adaptation of Victoria Wood's beloved sitcom will have a run at the Manchester Opera House
evidence_packet.summary: The stage adaptation of Victoria Wood's beloved sitcom will have a run at the Manchester Opera House
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sue Cleaver hails Victoria Wood legacy as she joins Dinnerladies stage tour - BBC News Image caption, Victoria Wood wrote and played Brenda, the deputy canteen manager, in the BBC TV comedy show Dinnerladies Published 1 hour ago Actress Sue Cleaver has said Victoria Wood would be "over the moon" with a new stage adaptation of beloved sitcom Dinnerladies, which she hailed as "a celebration of her legacy". Best known as Eileen Grimshaw in ITV soap Coronation Street, Cleaver is among the famous faces joining the new production, which is the first to be commissioned by Wood's estate since her death in 2016 at the age of 62. The 63-year-old, who featured in the BBC show as a recurring character, will take the stage as cynical canteen worker Jean, who was played by Anne Reid in the show. She said the script it "blew her away" and that it had been "beautifully adapted" from Wood's show. The show, created, written and co-produced by Wood, aired on the BBC from 1998 to 2000 and followed the workplace dramas of the staff and regulars in a canteen at a factory in Manchester. More than 25 years on, Cleaver told BBC Radio Manchester the sitcom, which ran for two series was "observational comedy at its finest". She said: "I'm thrilled to be doing it. "It's such a celebration of Vic's work. It's about the celebration of her and her legacy. "I think she'd be over the moon and I'm very excited to be a part of it." Cleaver added: "There's no way [the audience] are not going to be able to enjoy this show. "It's a British classic and nobody writes the way Vic writes. "If you've never been in a theatre in your life, make this the one time that you do come because it won't let you down." title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest hears

evidence_packet.title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest hears
evidence_packet.lead: Michelle Pearson and her four children were murdered in an arson attack at their home in Walkden
evidence_packet.summary: Michelle Pearson and her four children were murdered in an arson attack at their home in Walkden
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest hears - BBC News Image source, Family photos Image caption, The four Pearson children died during the petrol bomb attack, and their mother died 20 months later. By Phil Cunliffe Reporting from Bolton Coroners' Court Published 5 October 2026 Four children had been "petrified" by a series of attacks on their home before a petrol bomb attack killed them all, an inquest has heard. Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, Lia, three, died at their home in Jackson Street in Walkden in Greater Manchester in December 2017. Their mother Michelle, 37, was badly burned and died in August 2019. The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court - scheduled to last eight weeks - heard that Michelle had told police she did not feel safe in the house, which had been covered in graffiti and had its windows smashed. Zak Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for the murder of the four children, and in 2021 also convicted of Michelle's murder. Bolland was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 40 years and Worrall was sentenced to life with a minimum of 37 years in jail. Two weeks before the fatal attack, Bolland smashed windows at the house with a hammer, leaving glass everywhere. In a statement read out to the inquest, relatives said Michelle was traumatised and the called police on five separate occasions. Her son Kyle – who escaped the blaze – said in a statement to the inquest that "the police didn't do anything". Image source, GMP Image caption, Michelle Pearson and her four children were murdered after an arson attack at their home in Walkden Michelle suffered 68% burns to her body and "clung on to life" until she died on August 25, 2019, around 20 months after the attack. title: Artist 'taking legal advice' over Tories' use of Andy Burnham portrait

evidence_packet.title: Artist 'taking legal advice' over Tories' use of Andy Burnham portrait
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester illustrator Stan Chow says he was not asked permission for use of his cartoon
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester illustrator Stan Chow says he was not asked permission for use of his cartoon
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An artist has said he is taking legal advice after accusing the Conservative Party of copying his portrait of Andy Burnham at their party conference People attending the event in Birmingham have been handed water bottles featuring the image and labelled "Bottler Burnham" and "0% strength" and sweets labelled "Andy Panders' People Pleaser Pick N Mix" Labour supporter Stanley Chow, who created the image for Burnham's 2021 mayoral campaign in Greater Manchester, has claimed the party did not ask for permission to use the image A Conservative Party spokeswoman said the bottles were not on sale and merely handed out to attending media in "goody bags" Manchester illustrator Chow said: "I was stunned and angry when I saw what they had done. It is childish from them. I am taking legal advice "I'm very disappointed. It's frustrating that an institution like the Conservative Party has no idea that they are infringing copyright."

title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

evidence_packet.title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk
evidence_packet.lead: BT's planned takeover of broadband operator TalkTalk is subject to regulator approval
evidence_packet.summary: BT's planned takeover of broadband operator TalkTalk is subject to regulator approval
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The takeover would end of months of speculation over the future of TalkTalk and mean services for its millions of customers will continue as normal BT boss Alison Kirkby said it provided "a safety net" for TalkTalk customers. The administrator, Alvarez & Marsal, said it also provided certainty for TalkTalk's 900 staff based in Salford, Greater Manchester However, Virgin Media called it a "stitch-up" which allows BT to "tighten its grip" over the market. The government has given itself the power to have the final say on the deal, citing its importance to vital public services TalkTalk has 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers across the UK BT's Kirkby told the BBC's Today programme: "Two and a half million customers, including vulnerable households, and key emergency services might have lost their services if Talk Talk had failed, which it was on track to do "So BT stepped in as we were the only viable option to take the business forward."

title: Man City TV presenter Natalie Pike's 'terrifying' stalker ordeal

evidence_packet.title: Man City TV presenter Natalie Pike's 'terrifying' stalker ordeal
evidence_packet.lead: The Manchester City pundit said her stalker appeared at Etihad Stadium where she was working
evidence_packet.summary: The Manchester City pundit said her stalker appeared at Etihad Stadium where she was working
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Man City TV presenter Natalie Pike's 'terrifying' stalker ordeal - BBC News Image caption, Natalie Pike described her ordeal as "crazy" and "terrifying" By Stewart Whittingham North West Published 5 October 2026 A football presenter has described a "terrifying" eight-month ordeal in which her stalker turned up at a Premier League match where she was working. Former BBC Radio Manchester presenter Natalie Pike said the man was arrested after she recognised him while she was broadcasting at Etihad Stadium before Manchester City played Newcastle United in February. Ms Pike, who covered Scotland during the World Cup in the United States this summer, now works as City's in-house presenter as well as on other channels. Her stalker was last week given a suspended prison sentence and issued with a restraining order. Ms Pike said she had been on a spa day when her hairdresser called and said two men had come in trying to find her home address in the Cheshire village where she lives. The 43-year-old said she trawled through her Instagram messages and was able to identify one of the men. A week later, Ms Pike saw him again while she was on the pitch at Etihad Stadium. She said he was arrested the following day. He was convicted of stalking on 25 September and, in addition to the 12-month prison sentence suspended for 18 months and restraining order, was told he must carry out rehabilitation activity and do 100 hours' community service. The BBC has agreed to Ms Pike's request not to name him. Image source, PA Media Image caption, Natalie Pike works for Manchester City She told BBC Breakfast: "It has been terrifying for the last eight months not knowing what is happening or what he might do, for my safety but also my son's safety. "It has caused extreme anxiety for my whole family. "

title: 'It started with a cup of tea - now we help thousands'

evidence_packet.title: 'It started with a cup of tea - now we help thousands'
evidence_packet.lead: Twenty-five years ago Victoria "put a kettle on" for her community.
evidence_packet.summary: Twenty-five years ago Victoria "put a kettle on" for her community. Now she helps more than 2,000 people
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When Victoria Armstrong moved to Manchester as a university student in the 1990s she started to notice there were people living in her community who "had no-one" "I spent the first six months just putting on a kettle and putting bread in the toaster," the 53-year-old said Victoria, originally from Oxford, who had moved to Gorton after enrolling as a Fine Art student at Manchester University, started to host people for a cup of tea at her local church once a week Later she made it an official charity, founding Oasis in 2001 "It started with cups of tea and toast," Victoria said. "Twenty-five years later and we have helped thousands of people." Oasis now has its own centre, with 19 staff and 90 volunteers, running education classes, a free cafe, crisis support services, job clubs and a charity shop

title: Train station returning to Cheadle after more than 100 years

evidence_packet.title: Train station returning to Cheadle after more than 100 years
evidence_packet.lead: Cheadle in Stockport has been without a train station since its original hub closed in 1917
evidence_packet.summary: Cheadle in Stockport has been without a train station since its original hub closed in 1917
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work is beginning on bringing a train station back to the heart of a Greater Manchester village more than a century after its original station closed Cheadle in Stockport had a station just off the high street up until 1917 Funding for a new hub, which would be built next to Alexandra Hospital, was given the green light in 2022, with planning permission granted in 2023 but concerns about its effect on the timetabling of trains elsewhere on the network led to delays Stockport Council said the issue had now been resolved and council leader Mark Roberts said it was "a hugely significant moment for Cheadle and for Stockport" "For years we've fought for this station because we know the difference it will make to residents, businesses and the future prosperity of the area," he added Roberts said he was delighted that the initial highways work could now start on site thanks to the persistence and partnership of all involved

evidence_packet.evidence_text: When Victoria Armstrong moved to Manchester as a university student in the 1990s she started to notice there were people living in her community who "had no-one" "I spent the first six months just putting on a kettle and putting bread in the toaster," the 53-year-old said Victoria, originally from Oxford, who had moved to Gorton after enrolling as a Fine Art student at Manchester University, started to host people for a cup of tea at her local church once a week Later she made it an official charity, founding Oasis in 2001 "It started with cups of tea and toast," Victoria said. Oasis now has its own centre, with 19 staff and 90 volunteers, running education classes, a free cafe, crisis support services, job clubs and a charity shop

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way The Mancunian Way: Uncertainty looms PLUS: The 'Colombian greasy spoon' News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 17:15, 05 Oct 2026 View 5 Images Piccadilly Gardens street food market (Image: Manchester Evening News) Falafel King has been trading at Piccadilly Gardens for a decade. The team see a flurry of customers six days a week in one of the city’s busiest spots and, if it was up to them, they would remain there But matters have been taken out of their hands. Manchester council is calling time on the Piccadilly Gardens street food market on October 22 Traders have been offered a space in Lincoln Square when the Christmas Markets open next month (and no, I can’t quite believe it’s that time of year either, with my phone telling me it’s 21C outside as I type) But beyond December 22, everything is up in the air. I spoke to many of the traders last week, who each seemed to have different ideas around what their future would look like in 2027 One trader said they might be reopening at Lincoln Square in February, another suggested March. Some traders said they weren’t sure if they would be reopening in Lincoln Square beyond the Christmas Markets at all. The council says it ‘understands their uncertainty’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Moss Side Moss Side off-licence sold 'homemade' rum cocktails as 'slush puppies', police tell Manchester council Details were shared at council licensing hearing Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:35, 06 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Rich An off-licence in Moss Side was found selling ‘homemade’ rum cocktails as ‘slush puppies’, with some of the product found stored in ‘jerry cans’ on the premises, according to a police report The drink, known as Rum Beats, was claimed in a Greater Manchester Police (GMP) report to have been made and sold at Richie and Nikki's Off Licence on Princess Road on an ‘industrial scale’ as a type of ‘Jamaican rum punch cocktail’ Details of the sales at the shop were shared in reports published in a public hearing on Monday (October 5) during a review of the premises licence by Manchester council. evidence_packet.lead: Wigan Wigan's bizarre fake news story about a GP surgery that sparked chaos MP Jo Platt said residents deserve accurate information, not 'fabricated headlines designed to cause confusion and concern' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 05 A ‘fabricated’ social media
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan Wigan's bizarre fake news story about a GP surgery that sparked chaos MP Jo Platt said residents deserve accurate information, not 'fabricated headlines designed to cause confusion and concern' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 05 A ‘fabricated’ social media
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan's bizarre fake news story about a GP surgery that sparked chaos MP Jo Platt said residents deserve accurate information, not 'fabricated headlines designed to cause confusion and concern' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 05 A ‘fabricated’ social media graphic designed to resemble a genuine news story has been corrected by a medical centre and a Wigan MP. Braithwaite Road Surgery in Lowton responded after graphic, containing a picture of the centre and suggesting it was being turned into a 15-bed HMO The image also contained the words ‘say local MPs’. A spokesperson for Braithwaite Road Surgery has addressed the issue and apologised to ‘any of our patients who may have been worried or distressed as a result of this’ They added: “We are aware of false information currently circulating suggesting that Braithwaite Road Surgery is to be converted into a 15-bed HMO “We would like to reassure our patients and the wider community that this is completely untrue. We understand that hearing or reading information of this nature may cause concern, particularly when it relates to a local healthcare service that patients rely upon “This false information has been generated by a third party. We would encourage patients and members of the community to rely on information provided directly by the surgery or other official sources, rather than unverified information circulating on social media

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Inquest hears horrific threats Michelle Pearson received in weeks before petrol bomb murders An inquest into Michelle Pearson's death has heard she did not feel safe News Paul Britton Reporter 05:57, 06 Oct 2026 Updated 07:39, 06 Oct 2026 View A mum murdered with four of her children in a petrol bomb attack on their home told authorities she felt she was 'in danger' weeks before the tragedy, an inquest was told A neighbour of Michelle Pearson - who died in hospital 21 months after her children passed away - said the mum-of-six was 'at her wit's end with all of it' after previous attacks on their home, a coroner heard Ms Pearson, the inquest heard, told social workers that she did not feel safe in her own home, Jackson Street in Walkden , Salford . She also told Salford Council's housing department that threats against her had been made before the fatal blaze and that 'she was in danger', Bolt In a statement read to the inquest, the family said she asked the council to be moved, but was told she 'did not meet the criteria for emergency housing'. The inquest heard that before the fatal fire, the fire service had also sealed up her letter-box and discussed an escape plan The family said in the statement that Ms Pearson told her sister that she had asked the police for an injunction against Zak Bolland, preventing him from contacting her and her children

The airport has said it is 'reviewing' traffic management as taxis and private hire vehicle firms speak out, but there is a reason behind the increased congestion last m Comments News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 05:55, 06 Oct 2026 If you flew from Manchester Airport in September, you may have noticed something. The airport and the roads surrounding it were incredibly busy It’s something you may expect during the peak summer travel season, but it might take you by surprise once the schools go back at the start of autumn. Taxi firms and private hire vehicles have spoken out about the issue, claiming that they faced waits of up to 30 minutes to get t Many took to social media to voice their complaints. Blackpool-based taxi firm Mark’s taxis shared images of traffic at the airport on TikTok on September 25 with the caption: “Another day another complete shambles at Manchester Airport. It has taken 20 minutes to get out of the A spokesperson from Manchester Airport explained that there had been some traffic issues caused by a ‘range of factors’, and that measures were taken to help traffic flow, which has since returned to normal. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ancoats Demolition work begins on 'Holy Grail' church in Ancoats The church was built back in 1840 News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 20:25, 05 Oct 2026 View 2 Images All Souls Church on Every Street Demolition work on a historic Grade II listed church has begun. Pictures from the site show the sections of the All Souls Church on Every Street torn down on Monday (October 5) The works comes after residents complained of the state of the building which has become dilapidated over the years. The building was built in 1840 and is believed to have closed in the 1980s It was used as a joinery workshop for a short while after, but has since fallen into disuse. Last month, the Manchester Evening News, spoke to residents living around the building who said they had made complaints about its deteriorating condition, describing it as an “eyesore” In 2003, the building was placed on the SAVE Britain’s Heritage's, Buildings at Risk register. The group is a charity that campaigns for the preservation of threatened historical buildings in the country View 2 Images Crews are dismantling the historic church

Paul Gregory Blain sadly died on Monday (September 7) From Ordsall, Blain was the vice chairman of the Salford Children's Holiday Camp, affectionately known as the 'Jam Butty Camp'. The group was responsible for taking several impoverished Salford youths on trips to a holiday camp in Prestatyn, Wales The scheme has been in operation since 1926, giving thousands of young people respite from inner city life. A funeral service for Paul will be held at Agecroft Crematorium on Friday (October 9) Chairman Nick Abbott stated: "Ordsall and Salford have lost a giant of a man. One of the kindest, caring and loyal friends you could ever wish for. My heart aches for Kerry, his wife, and their children and grandchildren “Paul was the inspiration behind Salford by the Sea – Salford Children’s Holiday Camp. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:26, 05 Oct 2026 A man claimed he suffered a ‘horrifying’ ordeal during an alleged assault by door staff outside a Manchester nightclub. Gareth Evans spoke at a council licensing meeting which was open to the public on Monday (October 5), saying the alleged attack happened in December 2023 outsid The council meeting was called after Mr Evans applied for a review of the venue’s premises licence, claiming it ‘failed to uphold the licensing objectives of the prevention of crime and disorder, and public safety’ In a statement submitted to the hearing, the alleged victim claimed he was ‘subjected to a violent assault by door staff at the premises’ when he was placed in a ‘chokehold resulting in loss of consciousness and requiring paramedic attendance’ The incident was reported to Greater Manchester Police (GMP) but Mr Evans told the council hearing that ‘no further action’ was taken by the force He claimed CCTV footage of the alleged incident was ‘intentionally deleted or not saved to protect the door staff’ after it took place

She ho News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 18:08, 05 Oct 2026 Updated 18:59, 05 Oct 2026 "This is it. This is the day I die." Nicole Miller was broken. She feared that following a nine-month campaign of abuse and violence at the hands of her thug ex-partner, she wouldn't make The young mother, sat in their Wythenshawe flat, thought to herself: "If I don't get out, then I'm never going to get out." Nicole's ordeal, living under the control of Elliot Bulman, had become too much to bear She was abused when pregnant. She was abused while caring for their newborn child. She was attacked, raped and strangled. She was degraded Finally, she found the strength to escape. Nicole has now bravely spoken of her nightmare after Bulman was jailed. She has waived her automatic right to anonymity as the victim of sexual offences so her story can be told, in the hope of inspiring others to get their lives back Bulman, 22, of Peel Hall Road, Wythenshawe, was locked up for 15 years - and handed an additional five years on licence after being assessed as presenting a high risk of committing sexual offences and a high risk of harm to partner - last week

News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 18:06, 05 Oct 2026 Updated 18:07, 05 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Three cannabis farms were fo Around £2 million worth of cocaine and three grow houses have been found following a stop and search in Middleton . The huge discovery was made after a 38-year-old man was arrested when drugs and cash were found during a stop and search on Sunday (October 4) Patrol officers from the Middleton Neighbourhood Policing Team spotted a suspicious vehicle parked on Cemetery Street, Middleton, and stopped the car. A search was carried out and they recovered a portion of class A drugs, scales, and cash A 38-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply class A drugs. He remains in custody for questioning, GMP says GMP says that further intelligence led to the search of three properties in Middleton, Chadderton and Oldham . A cannabis farm was found at each address, as well as 20 kilograms of suspected cocaine. All recoveries are due to be assessed further According to police, the estimated street value of the drugs is around £2m

The team see a flurry of customers six days a week in one of the city’s busiest spots and, if it was up to them, they would remain there But matters have been taken out of their hands. Manchester council is calling time on the Piccadilly Gardens street food market on October 22 Traders have been offered a space in Lincoln Square when the Christmas Markets open next month (and no, I can’t quite believe it’s that time of year either, with my phone telling me it’s 21C outside as I type) But beyond December 22, everything is up in the air. I spoke to many of the traders last week, who each seemed to have different ideas around what their future would look like in 2027 One trader said they might be reopening at Lincoln Square in February, another suggested March. Some traders said they weren’t sure if they would be reopening in Lincoln Square beyond the Christmas Markets at all. The council says it ‘understands their uncertainty’

evidence_packet.summary: Wigan Wigan's bizarre fake news story about a GP surgery that sparked chaos MP Jo Platt said residents deserve accurate information, not 'fabricated headlines designed to cause confusion and concern' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 05 A ‘fabricated’ social media
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Wigan's bizarre fake news story about a GP surgery that sparked chaos MP Jo Platt said residents deserve accurate information, not 'fabricated headlines designed to cause confusion and concern' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 05 A ‘fabricated’ social media graphic designed to resemble a genuine news story has been corrected by a medical centre and a Wigan MP. Braithwaite Road Surgery in Lowton responded after graphic, containing a picture of the centre and suggesting it was being turned into a 15-bed HMO The image also contained the words ‘say local MPs’. A spokesperson for Braithwaite Road Surgery has addressed the issue and apologised to ‘any of our patients who may have been worried or distressed as a result of this’ They added: “We are aware of false information currently circulating suggesting that Braithwaite Road Surgery is to be converted into a 15-bed HMO “We would like to reassure our patients and the wider community that this is completely untrue. We understand that hearing or reading information of this nature may cause concern, particularly when it relates to a local healthcare service that patients rely upon “This false information has been generated by a third party. We would encourage patients and members of the community to rely on information provided directly by the surgery or other official sources, rather than unverified information circulating on social media

evidence_packet.title: Moss Side off-licence sold 'homemade' rum cocktails as 'slush puppies', police tell Manchester council
evidence_packet.lead: Moss Side Moss Side off-licence sold 'homemade' rum cocktails as 'slush puppies', police tell Manchester council Details were shared at council licensing hearing Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:35, 06 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Rich An off-licence in Moss Side
evidence_packet.summary: Moss Side Moss Side off-licence sold 'homemade' rum cocktails as 'slush puppies', police tell Manchester council Details were shared at council licensing hearing Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:35, 06 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Rich An off-licence in Moss Side
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Moss Side Moss Side off-licence sold 'homemade' rum cocktails as 'slush puppies', police tell Manchester council Details were shared at council licensing hearing Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:35, 06 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Rich An off-licence in Moss Side was found selling ‘homemade’ rum cocktails as ‘slush puppies’, with some of the product found stored in ‘jerry cans’ on the premises, according to a police report The drink, known as Rum Beats, was claimed in a Greater Manchester Police (GMP) report to have been made and sold at Richie and Nikki's Off Licence on Princess Road on an ‘industrial scale’ as a type of ‘Jamaican rum punch cocktail’ Details of the sales at the shop were shared in reports published in a public hearing on Monday (October 5) during a review of the premises licence by Manchester council. The shop's premises licence was temporarily suspended at a previous hearing in September It was said during the hearing on Monday that the Rum Beats cocktails were made by mixing Wray and Nephew, a 63 per cent alcohol volume Jamaican rum, with fruit juice, and that the drinks were usually sold by the business at events and fairs GMP said in their report: “Officers described the production process as homemade and unsophisticated, and could see no evidence of any quality control measures, appropriate hygiene measures, or equipment to establish accuracy or consistency within production.”

The airport has said it is 'reviewing' traffic management as taxis and private hire vehicle firms speak out, but there is a reason behind the increased congestion last m Comments News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 05:55, 06 Oct 2026 If you flew from Manchester Airport in September, you may have noticed something. The airport and the roads surrounding it were incredibly busy It’s something you may expect during the peak summer travel season, but it might take you by surprise once the schools go back at the start of autumn. Taxi firms and private hire vehicles have spoken out about the issue, claiming that they faced waits of up to 30 minutes to get t Many took to social media to voice their complaints. Blackpool-based taxi firm Mark’s taxis shared images of traffic at the airport on TikTok on September 25 with the caption: “Another day another complete shambles at Manchester Airport. It has taken 20 minutes to get out of the A spokesperson from Manchester Airport explained that there had been some traffic issues caused by a ‘range of factors’, and that measures were taken to help traffic flow, which has since returned to normal. They added that they are “carrying out an extensive review of the system View 3 Images TikTok user @marks.taxis shared images of traffic around the airport in September (Image: TikTok / @marks.taxis)

Cordons were placed around Corporation Street with fire crews on the scene for around one hour A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said: “At around 10pm this evening (Monday 5 October), two fire engines from Manchester Central , and the Technical Rescue Unit from Ashton Community Fire Station were called to reports of a person at height on “Crews arrived quickly and worked with Greater Manchester Police to make the area safe. One person was transferred into the care of North West Ambulance Service “Fire fighters were in attendance for around one hour.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Swinton Much-loved teacher retires from the Salford school where she's spent her entire 45-year career She was a newly-qualified teacher in her twenties when she arrived at the secondary school View 6 Images Teacher Sue Kirk retiring after 45 years at Comments News Emma Gill Parents editor 17:49, 05 Oct 2026 Updated 22:09, 05 Oct 2026 When Sue Kirk first arrived at Moorside High School as a newly qualified teacher she never imagined it would be the place she'd spend her entire teaching career Yet last week, the 'legendary' Mrs Kirk, who some students will also remember as Miss Crabbe, led a conga out of the school as she retired after an incredible 45 years The Swinton school was on the opposite side of the East Lancashire Road in Salford when she started there, initially travelling from Bradford before eventually settling in the area herself "It was my first teaching role and I taught girls PE," said Sue, who counts footballer Ryan Giggs among the pupils she's taught, revealing 'he was the fastest runner I ever saw' "I walked into that building with a leaky roof and narrow corridors and for some reason I never wanted to leave."

evidence_packet.summary: Politics Conservatives pledge £10 billion 'iron dome' defence system funded by two-child benefit cap 'Keeping Britain safe cannot be another promise for some distant point in the future' Comments News Nina Lloyd (PA) and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter The Conservative party have p
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Conservatives pledge £10 billion 'iron dome' defence system funded by two-child benefit cap 'Keeping Britain safe cannot be another promise for some distant point in the future' Comments News Nina Lloyd (PA) and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter The Conservative party have pledged a £10 billion 'iron dome' defence system to protect the UK and its sovereign territories in the face of what they have called 'science fiction'-style threats to Britain's safety The 'Britannia Shield' would be able to detect incoming strikes via a network of radar, command and control systems - and would be funded by reinstating the two-child benefit cap and reforming housing benefit, the Conservatives said "The world will not wait for Britain to get ready," leader Kemi Badenoch is to tell the party conference in Birmingham tomorrow (October 6). "War has returned to Europe. Missiles and drones are transforming warfare in the Middle East “Cheap weapons can now threaten cities, military bases and critical infrastructure in ways that would have sounded like science fiction a generation ago "The threat is here. Britain must be ready. And Britannia Shield will help make sure we are.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Data Journalism Manchester's population is shrinking as thousands leave - see how your area is changing The population of Greater Manchester increased by 0.6% last year Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter and Richard Ault (Reach Data Unit) 17: New data paints a complex picture of Greater Manchester's shifting demographics as the region's population increases by almost double the UK rate - at the same time as the city centre appears to be beginning to shrink Some 11,814 people moved out of the city of Manchester to other areas in the UK between mid 2024 and mid 2025, according to new estimates from the Office of National Statistics. That represents a net decline of 0.06pc, around 341 people Among possible factors for the exodus could be graduates leaving university, or priced-out Mancs leaving the city centre for the - in theory - cheaper suburbs Recent data analysed by the Manchester Evening News showed that the average rental price for a one-bedroom flat is now £1,003 per month - up 4.2pc from the previous year The nine other Greater Manchester boroughs saw a slight population increase of around or just under one percent, well above the national average rise of just 0.33pc, its lowest rate for nearly 30 years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ancoats Demolition work begins on 'Holy Grail' church in Ancoats The church was built back in 1840 News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 20:25, 05 Oct 2026 View 2 Images All Souls Church on Every Street Demolition work on a historic Grade II listed church has begun. Pictures from the site show the sections of the All Souls Church on Every Street torn down on Monday (October 5) The works comes after residents complained of the state of the building which has become dilapidated over the years. The building was built in 1840 and is believed to have closed in the 1980s It was used as a joinery workshop for a short while after, but has since fallen into disuse. Last month, the Manchester Evening News, spoke to residents living around the building who said they had made complaints about its deteriorating condition, describing it as an “eyesore” In 2003, the building was placed on the SAVE Britain’s Heritage's, Buildings at Risk register. The group is a charity that campaigns for the preservation of threatened historical buildings in the country View 2 Images Crews are dismantling the historic church

Paul Gregory Blain sadly died on Monday (September 7) From Ordsall, Blain was the vice chairman of the Salford Children's Holiday Camp, affectionately known as the 'Jam Butty Camp'. The group was responsible for taking several impoverished Salford youths on trips to a holiday camp in Prestatyn, Wales The scheme has been in operation since 1926, giving thousands of young people respite from inner city life. A funeral service for Paul will be held at Agecroft Crematorium on Friday (October 9) Chairman Nick Abbott stated: "Ordsall and Salford have lost a giant of a man. One of the kindest, caring and loyal friends you could ever wish for. My heart aches for Kerry, his wife, and their children and grandchildren “Paul was the inspiration behind Salford by the Sea – Salford Children’s Holiday Camp. News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 18:06, 05 Oct 2026 Updated 18:07, 05 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Three cannabis farms were fo Around £2 million worth of cocaine and three grow houses have been found following a stop and search in Middleton . The huge discovery was made after a 38-year-old man was arrested when drugs and cash were found during a stop and search on Sunday (October 4) Patrol officers from the Middleton Neighbourhood Policing Team spotted a suspicious vehicle parked on Cemetery Street, Middleton, and stopped the car. A search was carried out and they recovered a portion of class A drugs, scales, and cash A 38-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply class A drugs. He remains in custody for questioning, GMP says GMP says that further intelligence led to the search of three properties in Middleton, Chadderton and Oldham . A cannabis farm was found at each address, as well as 20 kilograms of suspected cocaine. All recoveries are due to be assessed further According to police, the estimated street value of the drugs is around £2m

evidence_packet.lead: The Mancunian Way The Mancunian Way: Uncertainty looms PLUS: The 'Colombian greasy spoon' News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 17:15, 05 Oct 2026 View 5 Images Piccadilly Gardens street food market (Image: Manchester Evening News) Falafel King has been trading at Piccadilly Garde
evidence_packet.summary: The Mancunian Way The Mancunian Way: Uncertainty looms PLUS: The 'Colombian greasy spoon' News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 17:15, 05 Oct 2026 View 5 Images Piccadilly Gardens street food market (Image: Manchester Evening News) Falafel King has been trading at Piccadilly Garde
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way The Mancunian Way: Uncertainty looms PLUS: The 'Colombian greasy spoon' News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 17:15, 05 Oct 2026 View 5 Images Piccadilly Gardens street food market (Image: Manchester Evening News) Falafel King has been trading at Piccadilly Gardens for a decade. The team see a flurry of customers six days a week in one of the city’s busiest spots and, if it was up to them, they would remain there But matters have been taken out of their hands. Manchester council is calling time on the Piccadilly Gardens street food market on October 22 Traders have been offered a space in Lincoln Square when the Christmas Markets open next month (and no, I can’t quite believe it’s that time of year either, with my phone telling me it’s 21C outside as I type) But beyond December 22, everything is up in the air. I spoke to many of the traders last week, who each seemed to have different ideas around what their future would look like in 2027 One trader said they might be reopening at Lincoln Square in February, another suggested March. Some traders said they weren’t sure if they would be reopening in Lincoln Square beyond the Christmas Markets at all. The council says it ‘understands their uncertainty’

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Latest Nine Gille and Marc Sculptures Bring Endangered Wildlife to the Heart of... . . Latest . Nine Gille and Marc Sculptures Bring Endangered Wildlife to the Heart of Manchester. By. About Manchester - . . October 5, 2026 0 . . . . . . Facebook. . Twitter. . Google+. . Pinterest. . WhatsApp. . . . . . . Nine striking sculptures by internationally acclaimed artists Gille and Marc will bring some of the world’s most endangered animals into the heart of Manchester this autumn, as ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ becomes part of Spinningfields.. . Running from October 2026 to October 2027, the year-long public art exhibition will see giant tortoises, elephants, hippos, tigers, gorillas and Javan rhinos take up residence across Spinningfields, transforming the city centre into an urban landscape where art and wildlife conservation meet.. . The exhibition is rooted in the idea that some of the greatest sources of wonder come from the natural world. Yet the planet is experiencing its sixth mass extinction, with thousands of species facing increasing threats to their survival.. . More than half of the £130.7m is accounted for by Universal Credit, with £68.2m spent in Altrincham and Sale West and 5,630 households claiming the benefit. A further £33.6m is spent on Personal Independence Payment (PIP), which helps people with the additional costs associated with long-term physical or mental health conditions or disabilities. There are 4,477 PIP claimants in the constituency. The remaining total comprises £10.7m in Housing Benefit, £9m in Disability Living Allowance, £5.4m in Employment and Support Allowance and £3.8m in Carer's Allowance. The figures should not be interpreted as showing that everyone receiving the benefits is unemployed. Universal Credit can be paid to people in work, while PIP is not means-tested and can be claimed regardless of whether someone is working. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Best known as Eileen Grimshaw in ITV soap Coronation Street, Cleaver is among the famous faces joining the new production, which is the first to be commissioned by Wood's estate since her death in 2016 at the age of 62 The 63-year-old, who featured in the BBC show as a recurring character, will take the stage as cynical canteen worker Jean, who was played by Anne Reid in the show She said the script it "blew her away" and that it had been "beautifully adapted" from Wood's show The show, created, written and co-produced by Wood, aired on the BBC from 1998 to 2000 and followed the workplace dramas of the staff and regulars in a canteen at a factory in Manchester More than 25 years on, Cleaver told BBC Radio Manchester the sitcom, which ran for two series was "observational comedy at its finest" "It's such a celebration of Vic's work. It's about the celebration of her and her legacy

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, Lia, three, died at their home in Jackson Street in Walkden in Greater Manchester in December 2017 Their mother Michelle, 37, was badly burned and died in August 2019 The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court - scheduled to last eight weeks - heard that Michelle had told police she did not feel safe in the house, which had been covered in graffiti and had its windows smashed Zak Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for the murder of the four children, and in 2021 also convicted of Michelle's murder. Bolland was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 40 years and Worrall was sentenced to life with a minimum of 37 years in jail Two weeks before the fatal attack, Bolland smashed windows at the house with a hammer, leaving glass everywhere In a statement read out to the inquest, relatives said Michelle was traumatised and the called police on five separate occasions

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police said it received reports of a suspicious vehicle at about 18:00 BST on Friday One vehicle stopped at the Eccles Interchange junction was found to have about £100,000 in cash inside. Shortly afterwards a second vehicle - also travelling to Manchester - was pulled over by police and £60,000 was seized Men aged 37 and 61 were arrested on suspicion of money laundering and both remain in custody for questioning Sgt Laura Abram said: "We will not tolerate any form of criminality on our streets – from driving offences to suspected money-laundering and associated criminality." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cllr Thomas Robinson has been chosen as the new Deputy Leader of Manchester City Council He fills the role vacated by Cllr Garry Bridges when he was elected Leader earlier this month and will serve alongside the other Deputy Leader, Cllr Tracey Rawlins His portfolio responsibilities will include work and skills, crime and safety and emergency planning Cllr Robinson has served as Executive Member for Health and Social Care since 2022 overseeing the adult social care service which was recently rated ‘Good’ by the Care Quality Commission, and has represented Clayton and Openshaw as a councillor since 2021 Raised in Ardwick, he has deep roots in Manchester and his experience growing up in a council flat amid a supportive community has shaped his commitment to public service and building a city where everyone can thrive regardless of background “As a born and bred Mancunian, to become the Deputy Leader of our city is truly humbling. In supporting Councillor Bridges as Leader, I promise to continue to put the voices of our communities as the heart of every decision we take in their service.”

Four junctions will be upgraded to make it easier and safer for people on foot and riding bikes to travel around the town centre. Segregated cycle paths will create safer routes for people of all ages and are especially valuable for younger or less confident riders, who may not feel comfortable mixing with traffic. Throughout construction, traffic management will be in place to keep the public and workers safe, with disruption kept to a minimum. Funding was first granted in 2023 from the Greater Manchester Mayor’s Cycling and Walking Challenge Fund and the council carried out extensive consultation that helped shape the plans. But work was delayed by the need to prepare for the demolition and regeneration of Crompton Place. With the removal of Crompton Place now underway, work on the travel improvements can get underway and construction is scheduled to begin on October 12. Yet within a month of his release, he committed similar offences in Wigan Borough in September 2023. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. They’ll also be championing emerging artists and grass-roots venues Highlights include Thursday’s Chris Hawkins x SXSW stage, curated by Radio 6 Music DJ Hawkins and South by Southwest, you’ll get to see a bunch of new acts handpicked by the industry experts as being on the way up, including The K’s, Tom A. Smith, The Wran and more Dot to Dot festival have curated another stage, and they’re known for booking future headliners; their Nottingham and Bristol festival has featured Idles, Hard Life and London Grammar, all before they made it big. Manchester gets a taste of their booking talent at Beyond The Musi There’s loads more up-and-coming artists hand-selected for your listening pleasure across a bunch of venues around Manchester. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. evidence_packet.title: MD Comment: Reflections from Labour Conference 2026 - AI, devolution and growth | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
evidence_packet.summary: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

The next phase of AI is likely to be much less about what a model can demonstrate on a screen and much more about whether businesses can deploy it securel There is also an opportunity for Manchester and the wider North that goes beyond simply increasing AI adoption. The region already has strengths across advanced materials, computing infrastructure, cyber security, health innovation and emerging technologies such as quantum. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC JJ Gabriel's full career timeline from name change to shock Man United exit request JJ Gabriel has been in the spotlight since he was just nine, and the teenage wonderkid recently grabbed headlines for requesting to leave Manchester United Comm JJ Gabriel appeared to be on the cusp of making history at Manchester United. Instead, the 15-year-old wonderkid asked to leave Old Trafford last month, requesting that his academy registration be cancelled after a breakdown in his relationship with the club United were left stunned by the timing of the request as Gabriel had been included in Michael Carrick's squad to face Brighton in the Carabao Cup, where he was set to become the youngest competitive player in the club’s history The BBC reported that Gabriel and his representatives believe the promises made regarding his route to the first team have not been fulfilled. The teenager travelled with the squad for much of United’s pre-season but was given only eight senior minutes, against Atletico Madrid , Gabriel has not trained with United since scoring a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah on September 10 and has since travelled to Barcelona . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Renowned British vocal ensemble The Tallis Scholars, conducted by Peter Phillips, present one of the greatest masterpieces of the a cappella repertoire: Sergei Rachmaninov’s Vespers . Inspired by ancient Slavonic chant and Russian Orthodox traditions, the work remains a landmark Interwoven with Rachmaninov’s score are three contemplative works by Arvo Pärt — Tribute to Caesar , Da Pacem, Domine and O Holy Father Nicholas .
